entries.title: Genesis 11:1
segments: One language--one speech; these words denote union in counsel and in language.

entries.title: Genesis 11:3
segments:
Go to; come now. 
 
  Slime--for mortar; bitumen; a pitchy substance which they used for cement.

entries.title: Genesis 11:4
segments:
A name; a tower of renown, which may serve as a centre of unity. 
 
It is natural for men to seek to be distinguished, and as natural to seek it in a wrong way and for a wrong end.  In doing this they will be disappointed.  Would they be truly great, and permanently honored, which they may and ought to desire, they must seek these blessings, not in the indulgence of selfish gratification, but in learning and doing the will of God.

entries.title: Genesis 11:6
segments: Nothing will be restrained; if permitted to go on, they will accomplish their designs.

entries.title: Genesis 11:7
segments: Confound their language; by an influence from God their speech was confounded, and their counsels divided, so that they separated themselves into different famlies speaking different languages.

entries.title: Genesis 11:9
segments:
Babel; meaning confusion. 
 
The effects of the confusion of tongues are seen down to the present day, in the variety of languages which are spoken, and in the difficulty thus occasioned of holding conversation and communicating freely the knowledge which multitudes need, and without which they are exposed to perish.

entries.title: Genesis 11:10
segments: Shem; the progenitor of Abraham, whose history Moses, the writer of this book, is about to give.

entries.title: Genesis 11:26
segments:
Lived seventy years; and after that, 
 
  Begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran; but not, it is supposed, in this order.  Haran was the first-born, and Abram was the youngest.  He is mentioned first as Shem was,
, because from him was to spring the Messiah. See

entries.title: Genesis 11:28
segments: Ur of the Chaldees; a place it is supposed between the Tigris and the Euphrates, about four hundred miles north-east of Canaan.  This is the first time the Chaldees are mentioned in Scripture.  They lived in the north part of Mesopotamia, now Koordistan.  Afterwards they went south into the land of Shinar, which was afterwards called Chaldea and Babylonia.

entries.title: Genesis 11:29
segments: Sarai--Milcah; these are both supposed to have been daughters of Haran, the elder brother of Abram and Nahor.  If so, these two brothers married their nieces; but it seems that Haran and Abraham, though both sons of Terah, had not the same mother.

entries.title: Genesis 11:31
segments:
Into; towards. 
 
  Canaan; a country on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean sea. 
 
  Haran; a place in Mesopotamia between the rivers Euphrates and Chebar.  It is called in the New Testament, Charran.

The statements of the Old Testament are in various ways confirmed by the New, and thus they mutually support and illustrate each other; while both throughout have special reference to, and in numerous ways proclaim the dignity and show forth the glory of Jesus Christ.
